programme: SNAI1 and HDAC3 form the classic Snail–histone-deacetylase corepressor axis that silences CDH1 (both list SNAI1 also represses CLDN1/CLDN3), driving epithelial/endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and junctional breakdown; PIAS4 sits upstream as the SUMO ligase controlling this axis (SUMOylation of Snail-family factors, and specifically of ACE2 in the COVID record); NFKBIB and the macrophage master regulator MAFB supply the downstream/parallel inflammatory arm (NF-κB target tone via TNF/IL1B/CXCL8/PTGS2/NOS2, and monocyte-macrophage reprogramming) that follows barrier compromise.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, SNAI1-driven endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (39888478) and HDAC3-linked epigenetic reprogramming of TLR4/TNF promoters (36840831) contribute to vascular/epithelial barrier leak and inflammatory tone; PIAS4 restrains ACE2 SUMOylation, a step implicated in viral entry (36057605); MAFB reprograms alveolar and monocyte-derived macrophages and is directly tied to severe disease (37917179, 40365863).
role_in_b: In IBS, the same axis would operate as the molecular substrate of the 'leaky gut': SNAI1-type repression of junctional genes (its target list includes CLDN1/CLDN3) fits the documented loss of tight-junction proteins, HDAC-mediated epigenetic changes accompany stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity (35600618), and a MAFB signature appears in colonic mucosal immune populations in an IBS-D model (42449180), consistent with low-grade mucosal macrophage activation.
shared_axis: COVID-19 and IBS both feature a compromised epithelial/endothelial barrier with EMT-like transcriptional silencing of junctional genes and macrophage-driven low-grade inflammation; the same SNAI1/HDAC3/PIAS4 repressor module plus NF-κB tone (NFKBIB) and macrophage reprogramming (MAFB) could be redeployed at each barrier site — pulmonary/vascular in COVID-19, mucosal/colonic in IBS — even though nothing retrieved states this cross-disease link directly.
reasoning: The module is nameable from real, independently documented biology (SNAI1/HDAC3 co-repression of CDH1, PIAS4 SUMOylation of Snail/ACE2), and most carrying factors are solidly placed in at least COVID-19; but placement in IBS is thin (HDAC3 via a stress/histone-acetylation model, not barrier genes directly; SNAI1, PIAS4, NFKBIB have no IBS evidence at all) and MAFB is explicitly flagged discordant, so the cross-disease connection rests on the shared-biology inference (barrier failure + macrophage activation) rather than on retrieved material.
support: 36841549 — HDAC3 as a druggable target in COVID-19 (PROTAC design); 36840831 — HDAC3-linked TLR4/TNF promoter methylation changes in COVID-19; 35600618 — HDAC-related histone acetylation in a stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity (IBS-relevant) model; 39888478 — SNAI1 upregulation drives endothelial-mesenchymal transition in COVID-19; 36057605 — PIAS4 suppresses ACE2 SUMOylation, protecting against SARS-CoV-2 entry; 37917179 — MAFB shapes macrophage response and controls severe COVID-19; 40365863 — MAFB-linked reprogramming of alveolar macrophages in COVID-19; 39434885 — MAFB context in vaccine-induced B-cell repertoire analysis (COVID-19, tangential); 42449180 — MAFB appears in colonic mucosal single-cell profiling of an IBS-D model.
how_to_falsify: In colonic organoids/biopsies from IBS patients and SARS-CoV-2-infected airway/vascular endothelial cultures, run ChIP-seq for SNAI1, HDAC3 and PIAS4-dependent SUMOylation marks at CDH1/CLDN1/CLDN3; knock down SNAI1 or HDAC3 and measure barrier integrity (TEER/permeability) and CDH1 re-expression in both systems. If occupancy or repression of these junctional genes does not track with barrier loss in one or both tissues, or if MAFB ChIP targets in IBS mucosal macrophages show no overlap with its COVID myeloid targets (consistent with its flagged discordance), the shared-module account is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (COVID) vs colorectal (IBS) — anatomically mismatched, so any shared axis must work through circulating/tissue-resident myeloid and epithelial-barrier biology rather than shared cell identity. Only 16 patient-group comparisons drawn from just 2 independent cohort pairs back this account, a narrow base. Tissue-generic factors (NCOA1, ETS1, CEBPD, LITAF, TCF4, VDR, LEF1, EBF1, E2F3, FOXO3, SREBF2, DNMT1) were already stripped out, so the remaining concordance is not simply 'inflamed epithelium' boilerplate. MAFB is marked discordant — its recurrence does not mean identical downstream wiring in both diseases. NEUROG3 (strong, IBS-only, enteroendocrine differentiation) and BCL11A (COVID-only, erythroid/lymphoid genetic-risk axis) recur but represent separate mechanisms not integrated into this barrier/macrophage story. HOXC9, ESRRA, MLX, SOX8 and KLF7 have no literature grounding in either disease and are excluded from the account entirely.
